name: Karateka 7800 -- conversion recipe
what: a build recipe, not a copy: it says where each piece comes from
_how_to_use: You supply your own disk image and cartridge. Nothing copyrighted is
in this file -- only hashes, offsets and lengths.

a8disk.what: Karateka, Atari 8-bit, as an ATX disk image

cart7800.what: Karateka (NTSC) 7800 cartridge, for comparison and for anything reused from it

xegs.note: the 16-byte CART header is included in this hash; regions are measured from the start of the ROM, after it

boot-loader.what: the boot record and first-stage loader

art-201.what: sparse sectors; row correlation says 6 bytes/row

art-0BE00.what: strongest picture structure in the image, 20 bytes/row

_new: original files that ship with the recipe, because they are ours
_output: the sha256 the finished cartridge must have, once there is one
_look_in: paths are relative to this file, so a recipe in patches/ reaches the disk with ../../
_source_choice: The XEGS cartridge is the source, not the disk, and the numbers say why:
A cartridge has no loader, no decryptor and no disk I/O, so more of the
game is visible and less of it needs replacing. The disk stays listed
because it is the same game and useful for cross-checking.
_region_offsets: offsets in 'xegs' regions are into the ROM, i.e. the file minus its 16-byte CART header
